evidence.frequency_or_severity: Agents routinely code ahead, accept meaningless green tests, couple tests to implementation, and mix behavior with cleanup; these failures undermine correctness and maintainability.

job: Drive one predictable behavior at a time through a meaningful red, the smallest real green implementation, and optional green-state refactoring.

rejected_alternatives: A deterministic script cannot choose behavioral examples or observation boundaries.
Generic testing knowledge does not reliably enforce meaningful red-green-refactor discipline.

positive_triggers: Implement a predictable behavior using TDD.
Reproduce and fix a defect with a failing regression test.
A ship handoff requests behavior-mode implementation.
negative_triggers: Pure refactoring with no intended behavior change.
Architecture, product, deployment, or research work.
Emergent or nondeterministic output without a trustworthy executable oracle.
inputs: Repository test commands and relevant existing tests.
default: Add one behavior-focused test, observe the intended failure, make the smallest real passing change, and refactor only from green.
forbidden_effects: Write production behavior before a meaningful red when TDD applies.
Weaken assertions or paste actual output into expectations.
Disable existing checks or add test-only production branches.
Create mock-shaped architecture or speculative abstractions.
Claim tests establish architecture or production safety.
completion_checks: Every implemented behavior has meaningful failure and passing evidence.
Focused and relevant prior tests pass.
Tests observe behavior rather than private structure.
Discoveries and non-TDD risks are reported.
